independent_computation.identification: The leaf is an `amount` on a support-item/ally-support event in a scenario whose name pairs Black Cleaver with Bloodsong. Bloodsong (item id 3877) is the only support item in the cache that emits a per-champion `amount`-bearing debuff: its Spellblade passive inflicts 'Expose Weakness'.
independent_computation.sourced_formula: Bloodsong Spellblade (data/items.json id 3877, passives[0].branches[0]): '... If the target is a champion, inflict them with ''Expose Weakness'' for 4 seconds, causing them to take {{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage from all sources ({{fd|1.5}} second cooldown ...)'.
independent_computation.template_semantics: The wiki template {{rd|A|B}} is the melee/ranged split: A = melee, B = ranged. Corroborated against items whose split is independently known, all read out of the same cache: Ravenous Hydra Cleave {{rd|40% AD|20% AD}} (40% melee / 20% ranged), Eclipse Ever Rising Moon {{rd|6%|4%}} max-health damage, Death's Dance Ignore Pain {{rd|30%|10%}} damage-stored, Blade of the Ruined King Mist's Edge {{rd|9%|6%}} current-health, World Atlas / Runic Compass Shared Riches execute threshold {{rd|50%|30%}}.
independent_computation.arithmetic: Expose Weakness amp, melee wielder = 8% = 0.08 as a fraction. Ranged wielder = 5% = 0.05. The engine's leaf is a fraction (0.08), not a percent (8.0), consistent with the new value.
independent_computation.why_the_old_value_is_wrong: 0.30 appears nowhere in Bloodsong's cached text. It is exactly Black Cleaver's Carve cap: data/items.json 'Black Cleaver' passives[0].branches[0] — 'Each stack inflicts {{as|6% armor reduction}}, up to {{as|30%|armor}} at 5 stacks.' That is an ARMOR REDUCTION on a legendary bruiser item, a different quantity (resistance shred, applied via reduce_resistance per docs/math-foundations.md §2.2) than a support-item all-sources damage amplifier, and it is not a support event at all. 0.30 is therefore a cross-wired/stale value, not a defensible Expose Weakness amount.

sources_quoted.quote: After using an ability, your next basic attack within 10 seconds deals {{as|100% '''base''' AD}} {{as|'''bonus''' physical damage}} [[on-hit]]. If the target is a champion, inflict them with ''Expose Weakness'' for 4 seconds, causing them to take {{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage from all sources ({{fd|1.5}} second cooldown, starts after using the empowered attack).

Dealing {{as|physical damage}} to an enemy champion applies a stack of ''Carve'' for 6 seconds, stacking up to 5 times. Each stack inflicts {{as|6% armor reduction}}, up to {{as|30%|armor}} at 5 stacks.

Ravenous Hydra Cleave {{rd|40% AD|20% AD}}; Eclipse Ever Rising Moon {{rd|6%|4%}}; Death's Dance Ignore Pain {{rd|30%|10%}}; Blade of the Ruined King Mist's Edge {{rd|9%|6%}}; World Atlas Shared Riches {{rd|50%|30%}}

reduce_resistance(R, r_flat, r_pct): R ← R − r_flat; R ← R·(1 − r_pct/100) ... 'Black Cleaver average stacks' (ArmorReductionEffect.average_reduction) — used only to confirm that the Black Cleaver 30% lives on the resistance path, never as an all-sources damage amplifier. The document contains no Bloodsong / Expose Weakness / support-event formula, so items.json is the sole authority for this leaf.

Bloodsong atoms carry evidence 'passive:Spellblade' with empty parameters — the atom layer records no numeric amp, so it neither supports nor contradicts 0.08; the branch text is the only numeric source.

caveats: Melee/ranged dependency: the sourced value is 8% (0.08) when the Bloodsong holder is MELEE and 5% (0.05) when RANGED. I could not read the scenario's roster (tests/ and scripts/ are out of bounds for this oracle), so 0.08 is confirmed as a real, correctly-scaled sourced Bloodsong value and 0.30 is confirmed as not one; if the Bloodsong holder in cleaver_bloodsong_roster is a ranged champion, the correct leaf would be 0.05 and the change would be right in magnitude/source but wrong in the range branch. Recommend a one-line check of the scenario's support champion's attack type against this split.

Units: the leaf is a fraction (0.08 = 8%). If the surrounding stream stores percents elsewhere, the unit convention should be checked for consistency — but 0.3 vs 0.08 are both fraction-shaped, so the change did not alter units.
